headline: 20 Bangladeshis killed in Russia-Ukraine war after being trafficked
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) reveals that men recruited for construction jobs were forced to fight in the invasion of Ukraine.
details: Twenty of 30 Bangladeshis allegedly recruited for construction jobs in Russia have been killed after being forced to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war, according to the Special Response Battalion (SRB).
Additional DIG Asaduzzaman, commander of SRB-10, announced that 17 of the victims died in a drone strike on their first day at the front, while three others died later.

The investigation began after the father of Rajon Hossain, 21, filed a case. Rajon returned to Bangladesh on August 23 with severe injuries, including a fractured pelvis that left him unable to move his legs.
Investigators say a trafficking network involving people in Russia and Kyrgyzstan recruited young men from nine districts through three companies: Jabal-e-Nur, RS International, and TS Group.

Rajon was allegedly charged Tk 825,000 for a promised construction job. After arriving in Russia on May 7, he and 30 others were forced into the Russian Army and given 21 days of training before being sent to the front.
After being hit by a drone strike, Rajon reportedly crawled four kilometres to reach a camp and spent four days struggling to reach a hospital before escaping with embassy assistance.

Two alleged recruiters, Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher Lentu, were arrested on Tuesday. The SRB says two returnees are recovering in Bangladesh, two are in a Moscow hospital, and six remain on the battlefield.
Investigators are continuing to search for other members of the trafficking network.

headline_marked: Spend 30-60 mins twice a week: [[PM urges people to clean areas to prevent dengue]]
headline: Spend 30-60 mins twice a week: PM urges people to clean areas to prevent dengue
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman called for collective citizen action to destroy mosquito breeding grounds and save lives from the disease.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has urged citizens to spend 30 to 60 minutes at least twice a week cleaning their homes and surrounding areas to combat the dengue situation.
In a video message posted on his verified Facebook page on Wednesday, the PM emphasized that the government cannot solve these problems alone and needs the collective effort of all citizens.

He highlighted that just as the people of all walks of life united for the independence of 1971, the anti-autocracy movement of 1990, and the 2024 mass uprising, they can now unite to solve national health crises.

The Prime Minister noted that the most effective way to prevent dengue is to destroy the breeding grounds of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically by removing stagnant water and accumulated waste from every corner of the houses and streets.
Regarding dengue vaccines, the PM stated that while vaccines have been discovered, their effectiveness has shown limitations in various tests, making cleanliness the primary defense.

He praised the efforts of nearly 25 million students and 4 million members of organizations like BNCC, Scouts, Girl Guides, and Red Crescent, who have been cleaning districts and upazilas every Saturday for the past month.
The PM concluded by stating that a government is successful only when it works together with the people, and that collective action can save many lives from the 'curse' of dengue.
